vocabulary.meaning: to drink a large amount very quickly
examples: He chugged the drink in a few seconds.
Doctors warn against chugging large amounts of alcohol.

vocabulary.meaning: drinking a large amount of alcohol in a short period
examples: Binge drinking can lead to serious health and safety risks.
Campaigns try to reduce binge drinking among young adults.

vocabulary.meaning: affected by alcohol or drugs so that normal behaviour and judgement are reduced
examples: The driver was heavily intoxicated.
An intoxicated person may make unsafe decisions.

vocabulary.meaning: the amount or act of drinking alcoholic beverages
examples: Health agencies publish guidance on alcohol consumption.
Excessive alcohol consumption can damage the liver.

vocabulary.meaning: a standard measure used to compare the amount of pure alcohol in drinks
examples: The label shows how many units of alcohol the bottle contains.
People often underestimate how many units of alcohol they drink.

vocabulary.meaning: influence from other people of the same age or social group
examples: Peer pressure can encourage risky drinking.
She refused the drink despite peer pressure.

vocabulary.meaning: a condition in which the body loses too much water
examples: Alcohol can contribute to dehydration.
Drink water to reduce dehydration after exercise.

vocabulary.meaning: unpleasant symptoms experienced after drinking too much alcohol
examples: He woke up with a terrible hangover.
A hangover can include headache and nausea.

vocabulary.meaning: the practice of avoiding excessive amounts
examples: Doctors often advise drinking in moderation.
Moderation is important when consuming alcohol.

vocabulary.meaning: behaviour involving actions that may be dangerous
examples: Alcohol can increase risk-taking behaviour.
Young people may underestimate the consequences of risk-taking.
